name: quote

changes.note: Fix: every quote after the first on a page drew the nested mark (‘ instead of “), because open-quote raised the quote depth and nothing lowered it. An absolutely positioned no-close-quote on ::after lowers it without adding a grid row.

description: A quotation and its attribution — testimonial, pull quote or featured endorsement — as a native figure/blockquote/figcaption. Plain, card and editorial pull variants, three sizes, an optional avatar and rating, and a large decorative opening mark in the document language's own quotation glyph. The card variant reads the card aliases, so themes restyle both together.

text.description:
The quotation itself. Put one or more

inside; do not type quotation marks — the decorative mark is drawn by the stylesheet.

author.description: Attribution: an optional media part followed by name and role.

media.description: Inside author: wrapper for a nested data-ui="avatar" (or a logo image). The avatar keeps its own data-size.

role.description: Inside author: title, company or source.

--quote-accent.description: Colour of the opening mark and of the pull variant's rule (custom property). Pass a colour token.

required_attrs: the quotation in a <blockquote>, the attribution in the figure's <figcaption>
alt text on any image inside the media slot
a11y.notes: figure + blockquote + figcaption is the native quotation pattern: assistive technology announces the blockquote and associates the caption with the figure. The large opening mark is generated content with an empty text alternative; do not add literal quotation marks to the text as well.

notes: A nested data-ui="rating" goes directly in the figure, before the text; it is a component of its own, not a part.
The avatar sits inside [data-part="media"] and keeps its own five-attribute contract — its data-size belongs on the avatar, never on the part.
A wall of testimonials is the testimonials pattern: card quotes in a grid, columns or a marquee.
The pull variant belongs inside long-form content (the article pattern), between paragraphs.
